parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic بَرْزَخ (barzaḵ), from Parthian *bwrz-ʾxw (/⁠burz-axw⁠/), from Parthian bwrz (/⁠burz⁠/, “high”) + ʾxw (/⁠axw⁠/, “world”).

Borrowed from Arabic تَاج (tāj), from Parthian *𐫤𐫀𐫃 (*tʾg /⁠tāg⁠/, “crown”), attested in 𐫟𐫀𐫡𐫤𐫀𐫃 (xʾrtʾg /⁠xārtāg⁠/, “crown of thorns”). Related to Persian تخت (taxt, “bed, throne”), and akin to Old Armenian թագ (tʻag), Arabic تاج (tāj), and Aramaic תָּגָא (tāḡā), Iranian borrowings.
